purpose: Compare the user-completed g461 physical round trips with matched local source/receiver profiles.
method: Filter exact build, source/receiver roles and cutoff, then match exchangeTag; use local elapsed spans, never subtract clocks across laptops. Zero timing with a measured bit is a valid sub-resolution observation. Startup/native spans overlap and are not additive.

interpretation.coldPreparation: Two unprepared entries dominate readiness outliers; prepared entries still wait for authenticated native-pair readiness. Persistent warm workers are a candidate, not an implemented or validated fix.
interpretation.capture: Foreground takes 1-10ms or 10-100ms in this cohort; no fallback observed. Capture is not zero-cost, but it cannot explain the cold B readiness outliers.
interpretation.apply: The 337300us receiver dispatch contains a 334ms worker apply span. That span can include nested child IPC and authority work; it does not isolate SendInput or prove a pointer queue backlog.
interpretation.failures: No fault/session_failed/poison event inside the actual crossing cohort. Earlier post-repair faults are reported separately; current READY does not establish a fix for intermittent disconnects.
interpretation.safety: Do not suppress authority checks, ignore retirement failures, extend trust freshness or preserve a TLS connection without verified input release merely to reduce timings.
interpretation.comparison: g459 sample and g461 sample have different cadence and system conditions. This diagnostic-only change establishes no causal latency improvement.

validation.pairedData: All 13 exchange tags uniquely pair source and receiver; all complete with end=ok.
validation.runtime: Both collected protected services and input health READY.
validation.software: No runtime source changed in this acceptance analysis; rebuild, package tests and reinstall skipped.
validation.pending: No latency fix or additional deployment performed.
